title: How long does a fitted furniture project actually take?
description: From first contact to finished installation. A realistic timeline for a bespoke fitted furniture project, with honest explanations for each stage.
author: Sturij

standfirst.text: From first contact to finished installation. A realistic timeline for a bespoke fitted furniture project, with honest explanations for each stage.

body.text: The most common question after 'how much will it cost' is 'how long will it take.' The honest answer is typically 4-8 weeks from confirmed order to completed installation. That range feels wide, so here's what determines where your project falls within it.
body.heading: The honest answer

body.text: There are four stages, and each has its own timeline: design and specification, material ordering, manufacture, and installation. Some overlap; some can't start until the previous stage completes.

Design and specification typically takes 1-2 weeks. This includes the survey visit, proposal preparation, any revisions you request, and final sign-off. Some projects are straightforward — a single fitted wardrobe with a clear brief might go from survey to confirmed specification in a few days. A multi-room project with several material options to compare and a layout to iterate might take two weeks of back-and-forth.
body.heading: Design and specification

body.text: The pace of this stage is largely in your hands. We don't rush it because the specification needs to be right — changes after materials are ordered cost time and money. Take whatever time you need to be confident in the design.

Material lead times are the variable most outside anyone's control. Standard Egger boards from UK stock typically arrive within 5-7 working days. Specialist decors or textures not held in UK warehouses can take 2-3 weeks. Blum hardware is usually available within a week. If your specification includes anything unusual — a specific handle from Häfele, a pull-out system from Kesseböhmer — lead times vary.
body.heading: Material lead times

body.text: We confirm exact lead times before you sign off the order, so there are no surprises. If a particular material has a long lead time, we'll flag it during specification so you can decide whether to wait or consider an alternative.

Manufacture depends on the project's complexity and scale. A single fitted wardrobe might take 2-3 days in the workshop. A full bedroom with wardrobes, bedside units, and a dressing area might take 5-7 days. A multi-room project is scheduled in sequence. Everything is manufactured to final dimensions — there's no 'assemble on site from flat-pack' stage.
body.heading: Manufacture and installation

body.text: Installation is the fastest stage. A single wardrobe installs in a day. A full bedroom is typically 2-3 days. Multi-room projects are scheduled room by room. Because the same person who manufactured the furniture is installing it, there's no waiting for a separate fitting team. And because everything was made to precise measurements, installation is assembly and scribing, not adaptation.
